proofSteps: Write the finite polynomials over O_E, then evaluate them in any O_E-algebra.

nodes.statement: If A is a π-torsion-free O_E-algebra with O_E-linear ring endomorphism σ lifting a↦a^q modulo π, the ghost map w_A is injective and its image consists precisely of sequences y with y_(n+1)-σ(y_n)∈π^(n+1)A for every n≥0.

proofSteps: Injectivity follows inductively by cancelling π^n in the nth coordinate.
The binomial congruence propagates a≡b mod π^i to a^q≡b^q mod π^(i+1).

nodes.statement: There is a unique functor W_(O_E,π) from O_E-algebras to O_E-algebras with underlying set A^N for which every ghost map is an O_E-algebra homomorphism. Its operations are universal integral polynomials and are natural even on algebras with π-torsion. For a π-adic input algebra this means the same functor, with its subsequently specified V-topology, not a new flat lift.

proofSteps: Apply Dwork to O_E[X_i,Y_i,…] with the coefficient-fixing Frobenius lift X_i↦X_i^q.
Solve addition, multiplication and scalar ghost equations there and establish integral coefficient polynomials.
Transfer the identities by natural evaluation to every A, including π-torsion.

nodes.title: Perfect ramified strict lift
nodes.statement: For every nonarchimedean local E with finite residue F_q and perfect F_q-algebra R, W_OE(R) is the unique π-adically complete π-torsion-free (hence O_E-flat) O_E-algebra with specified reduction W_OE(R)/π≅R. In characteristic zero it is canonically W(R)⊗_(W(F_q))O_E, already complete because O_E is finite free. In equal characteristic it is R[[π]]. Uniqueness is in the category of complete lifts with the fixed residue identification.

proofSteps: In mixed characteristic use VF=π and invertibility of F for perfect R to identify V^nW with π^nW; the expansion proves completeness and torsion-freeness.
Use Teichmuller limits to construct the unique residue-lifting map between two strict lifts.
Compare with scalar extension through the unramified coefficient subring; a finite basis preserves π-adic completeness.
In equal characteristic the coefficient embedding gives R[[π]], with coefficientwise q-Frobenius.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate Teichmuller lift
nodes.statement: If Q≡πX mod X² and Q≡X^q mod π, its Lubin–Tate formal group satisfies LT_Q([x]_Q,[y]_Q)=[LT_Q(x,y)]_Q when perfect A is complete for (x,y). For a perfect complete valued field F of characteristic p and any Lubin–Tate formal group LT over O_E, the weak limit [x]_LT=lim_n[π^n]_LT([x^(q^(−n))]) gives an injective O_E-module map (m_F,+_LT)→(W_OE(m_F),+_LT). This is a module map for the formal-group law, not for ordinary addition.
hypotheses: E characteristic zero for this cited arbitrary Witt functor; x,y topologically nilpotent. The general formal power series require the weak topology, not solely π-adic convergence.
proofSteps: Identify ([x]_Q,[y]_Q,π) with ([x],[y],π) and prove the needed complete topology.
Evaluate the formal group using completeness and commute it with Q iterations.
Apply the limit characterization of [−]_Q, then the identical contraction argument for a general LT formal power series.
The residue map proves injectivity and scalar compatibility.
acceptance: State the coefficient field, formal group and topology in the limit; no ordinary additive-map assertion.

nodes.title: Perfectoid root extension and split sheaf descent
nodes.statement: The charts B_n are sheafy. Their completed extension to E_root∞ is perfectoid; the associated perfected disc charts glue to S×_(F_q)Spa F_q[[t^(1/p^∞)]]. Hence curly-Y_S is an analytic adic space over O_E. In mixed characteristic the charts are sousperfectoid; in equal characteristic perfection after the root extension and the split-module argument give the same sheaf conclusion.
hypotheses: B_n as defined above; plus rings are integral closures. The splitting is a continuous B_n-linear retraction, not a ring retraction.
proofSteps: Reduce to n=1 using coefficient perfection and Frobenius.

For A_0^+, use u=[ϖ]^(1/p): u^p divides p in mixed characteristic because π=[ϖ]s_0 and p is a unit times a power of π; the root presentation proves u is regular and Frob:A_0^+/u→A_0^+/u^p is bijective. Apply the integral-perfectoid criterion (BMS 3.10(ii)); in equal characteristic apply the perfect characteristic-p criterion.
Identify the tilt from the reduction presentation and t_1^sharp=π/[ϖ]. Normalize the global disc coordinate so these are the corresponding nested disc charts.
The coefficient-root extension admits a topological module splitting; transport it through the completed chart tensor product. Apply sousperfectoid sheaf descent, then glue the rational chart cover.
acceptance: Verify the chosen u and both quotient ideals in the criterion; establish a continuous splitting before invoking the imported theorem.

For ϖ,ϖ′ find n with ϖ|ϖ′^n and ϖ′|ϖ^n; the topologies and nonvanishing opens coincide.

nodes.statement: For n∈Z, descend the trivial line on Y_S with semilinear Frobenius operator Φ_n=π^(−n)φ to define O_X(n). The tensor comparison O(m)⊗O(n)≃O(m+n) and dual comparison O(n)^∨≃O(−n) preserve the descent trivializations. Its sections are exactly f∈O(Y_S) with φ(f)=π^n f. The rank-one coefficient operator π^(−n)σ has isocrystal slope −n; the geometric twist has degree n. The arbitrary-rank exact tensor functor has the sole VB1 owner.
hypotheses: Use the actual RF1 quotient and analytic invertible O-modules. No use of an arbitrary-rank isocrystal classification or a completed VB1 stage is required to define this rank-one descent.
proofSteps: Use local translate-disjoint opens in Y_S to descend the trivial line and its integral-power cocycle.
Multiplying the coefficients π^(−m)π^(−n) gives tensor and dual identifications.
A descended section is Φ_n-invariant, equivalently φ(f)=π^n f.
Compare the coefficient rank-one normalization with VB0’s isocrystal convention; export agreement to VB1 without importing the full functor.
acceptance: Use n=1 and n=−1 to test the sign; the full functor payload of the legacy id is forwarded.

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate divisor section
nodes.statement: Let E_LT∞ be the completion of the Lubin–Tate torsion tower, and S^sharp an untilt over it. A compatible nonzero torsion parameter X̃ gives a convergent period function f=Σ_(i∈Z)π^i[X̃^(q^(−i))] satisfying φ(f)=πf. Its zero on X_S is exactly the untilt divisor, with multiplicity one. Hence 0→O_X→O_X(1)→O_(S^sharp)→0, with the last map interpreted through the chosen divisor trivialization. Tensoring gives the corresponding consecutive-twist exact sequences.
hypotheses: The chosen LT tower is distinct from E_root∞. The all-E functional construction uses the LT logarithm; its mixed-characteristic period comparison has the precise SW13 input recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Use the LT Teichmuller lift and compatible torsion sequence to form the convergent bilateral sum. In mixed characteristic use the crystalline-boundary/Cech comparison first, together with the separately requested Lubin–Tate logarithm exact sequence; it does not depend on the resulting LT section.
Shift the summation index to prove the Frobenius eigenvalue.
Identify the function with the LT logarithm on the universal cover; the logarithm’s torsion zeros are simple.
Apply the generic Cartier ideal comparison to identify I_D(1) with O and deduce exactness.
acceptance: The product of two such sections at the same leg has a double zero; the one-section theorem is genuinely simple.

The analytic chart maps are constructed separately on U=⋃_gD(g). This node does not assert U=X_S or define an invertible degree-one Proj twist; both need the VB2:ampleness theorem.
hypotheses: The nonnegative grading is by N; O(n) exists for integral n. Proj need not be covered by degree-one generators.
proofSteps: Define the direct sum and multiplication using coherent tensor associativity of rank-one twists.
Use the existing graded-ring and ProjectiveSpectrum construction.
Identify standard degree-zero localization charts and their overlap maps.

nodes.title: Witt seminorm extension and restriction
nodes.statement: For a perfect F_p-algebra with a power-multiplicative seminorm α bounded by the trivial norm, define λ(α)(Σp^i[x_i])=max_i p^(−i)α(x_i), and μ(β)(x)=β([x]). They preserve multiplicative seminorms. The maps on their Berkovich spectra are continuous, μλ=id and λμ≥id. The same formulas extend to the relative integral and interval rings with the domination conditions of KL5.1.2.
hypotheses: The initial ring need not be a field or Banach. The later analytic relative version uses a perfect uniform Banach pair over an analytic field and 0<s≤r.
proofSteps: Use homogeneous Witt addition polynomials to prove the ultrametric bound.
A leading maximal coefficient gives multiplicativity when α is multiplicative; iterate for power multiplicativity.
Prove μ is subadditive despite the nonadditivity of Teichmuller representatives.
Use stable Witt presentations to prove continuity and μλ=id; extend bounded seminorms to completions.
acceptance: Distinguish a ring homomorphism from this construction on seminorms.

nodes.title: Relative extended Robba rings
nodes.statement: For a perfect uniform Banach pair (R,R^+) over an analytic field of characteristic p with spectral norm α, define Ẽ^int=W(R), Ẽ=Ẽ^int[1/p], R̃^(int,r)={Σ_(i≥0)p^i[x_i]:p^(−i)α(x_i)^r→0}, R̃^(bd,r)=R̃^(int,r)[1/p], R̃^r its Frechet completion for λ(α^s), 0<s≤r, and R̃^[s,r] its Banach completion for max(λ(α^s),λ(α^r)). Dropping r takes the union over r>0. Define each plus-input variant by R^+ instead of R. Its integral/bounded variants are W(R^+) and W(R^+)[1/p]; R̃^+ is the completion for all s>0, whereas R̃^∞=∩_rR̃^r is a different ring. Record p-adic, weak, Banach, Frechet and inductive limit topologies separately.

proofSteps: Use the coefficient norm estimates to show the growth subsets are subrings.
Localize integral growth rings and complete in the indicated families of norms.
Use log convexity to identify the interval norm with its two endpoint maximum.
Construct inclusions, their topologies and Frobenius φ:R̃^[s,r]≃R̃^[s/q,r/q].

nodes.title: Robba growth, units and Frobenius invariants
nodes.statement: For nonzero x, t↦log λ(α^t)(x) is convex. In R̃^r, boundedness as t→0 characterizes R̃^(bd,r). Every unit of R̃ is already a unit in R̃^bd by KL5.2.3. The φ^d-invariant ring is W(R^(φ^d))[1/p], retaining idempotents and disconnected constants. For R^+=R°, membership x∈R̃^+ within R̃^∞ is equivalent to limsup_(t→∞)λ_t(x)^(1/t)≤1.
hypotheses: Use exactly the bounded or completed ring in each criterion. Frobenius invariants are not asserted to be Q_p when the base is disconnected.
proofSteps: Prove convexity first on finite Witt sums and then by completion.
Use bounded endpoint norms to recover bounded Witt coefficients.
For a unit x with inverse y, use affine residue-field log norms and a uniform two-radius bound to show both x and y have bounded growth near zero.
For invariants compare each coefficient under φ^d; for the plus criterion use the integral/fractional splitting and the asymptotic coefficient maximum.

nodes.title: Controlled Robba splittings and intersections
nodes.statement: For 0<s≤r and n∈Z every x∈R̃^[s,r] splits x=y+z with y∈p^nR̃^(int,r), z extending to every [s,r′], r′≥r, and λ_t(z)≤p^((1−n)(1−t/r))λ_r(x)^(t/r) for t≥r. For 0<c<1 there is the second splitting of KL5.2.9 into bounded and plus parts with endpoint norm bounds and its φ estimates. Consequently R̃^[s,r]∩R̃^[s′,r′]=R̃^[s,r′] inside R̃^[s′,r] for 0<s≤s′≤r≤r′. Intersection preservation for a base ring square requires strict inclusions and, for completions, a strict difference map.
hypotheses: The interval intersection specifies its common ambient ring. The strictness conditions of Remark 5.2.13 cannot be removed.
proofSteps: Split finite Witt sums at their p-adic index, or by α(x_i)>c.
Approximate a completed element by a geometrically convergent sequence of bounded sums.
Sum the split pieces using the displayed estimates.
Apply the integral-ring intersection lemma and strict completion exactness to the interval and base-square intersections.

nodes.title: Positive Frobenius eigenvectors on a window
nodes.statement: For n≥0,d>0,q=p^d and r>0, restriction identifies {x∈R̃^+:φ^d x=p^n x}, {x∈R̃:φ^d x=p^n x}, and compatible eigenvectors on the fundamental window R̃^[r/q,r]. The window equality is interpreted by agreement after restriction to the overlap on which x and φ^d x are both defined. The all-E version has multiplier π^n and q-Frobenius. This is the concrete period-ring presentation of nonnegative-degree sections, without a finite-dimensionality assertion.
hypotheses: The displayed KL result has n nonnegative. Negative twists and geometric vanishing need their own arguments and cannot be inferred by changing this sign.
proofSteps: Iterate Frobenius and use interval intersections to extend a window eigenvector across all radii.
The eigenvalue gives the plus growth bound.
For a general R^+ use the residue projection in the final paragraph of KL5.2.12, rather than replacing R^+ by R°.
Compare the extended eigenvector with the invariant descent equation defining O(n).
In the growth estimate use an iteration index m distinct from the eigenweight n, as corrected in KLII Appendix A, printed p. 190.

The Kiehl property is proved for Ẽ^int and R̃^(int,r), and separately for R̃^[s,r]; it is not automatically asserted for all twelve variants.

Apply the controlled splitting to preserve its strictness under each completion.

nodes.title: Relatively perfectoid interval rings
nodes.statement: For 0<s≤r the Banach rings Ẽ, R̃^(bd,r) and R̃^[s,r] are relatively perfectoid. For any compatible adic plus extension they are stably uniform, sheafy, rationally acyclic and satisfy finite-projective Kiehl gluing. After scalar extension to the completed p-power-root tower the interval norm is power multiplicative and the ring is perfectoid. In all-E annular charts use the specified whole root relations and prove the coefficient extension of these norm estimates.
hypotheses: No field assumption on R. Relative perfectoidness is the imported sousperfectoid/relative-perfectoid condition, not an unproved designation for every Frechet or integral ring.
proofSteps: Compute scalar tensor norms using fractional p-power exponents and their orthogonal basis.
Prove power multiplicativity away from the finitely many norm-crossing radii and use convex continuity at crossings.
Frobenius-compatible Teichmuller representatives generate a dense perfect subring after tensor extension.
Apply the R5 split completed-base-change and sheafiness criterion to the listed Banach rings.
Use the corrected perfectoid completed-tensor comparison of KLII Theorem 3.3.13 (including injectivity), requested from P3, when invoking Lemma 5.3.14; the old KL3.6.11 proof is incomplete.
acceptance: The integral period disc uses its own chart theorem; it is not one of the three rings in this assertion.

nodes.statement: Give R̃^[s,r] the plus ring obtained by completing the subring generated by elements of endpoint norm <1 and [R^+]. A semivaluation first determines its unique exponent t∈[s,r], then a seminorm γ=μ(β)^(1/t) of R. Extending to H(γ) and using {x:v([x])≤1} yields the valuation on R. This defines μ_ad:Spa(R̃^[s,r],R̃^[s,r],+)→Spa(R,R^+) as a continuous map of adic topological spaces, without a structural ring homomorphism R→R̃^[s,r].
hypotheses: Teichmuller representatives are multiplicative; their nonadditivity must be handled through the valuation-ring criterion. The pair uses the specified completed plus ring.
proofSteps: Determine t by evaluating a topologically nilpotent unit from the analytic coefficient field.
Use domination to extend the seminorm to the completed residue field.
Prove the bounded Teichmuller representatives form a valuation ring.
Check the plus condition and continuity on rational inequalities.

nodes.title: Rational base change and interval descent
nodes.statement: A rational localization (R,R^+)→(S,S^+) induces the rational localization of interval pairs representing μ_ad^−1Spa(S,S^+). Rational base coverings therefore induce annular coverings and the interval period sheaf satisfies Kiehl gluing. For a finite covering I=⋃I_j of a compact interval in (0,∞), R̃^I→∏R̃^I_j is effective descent for finite projective modules. After the scalar extension of KL5.3.14, each subinterval restriction is itself a rational localization; before that extension use the proven gluing square, rather than asserting rationality.
hypotheses: The interval cover is finite and uses closed intervals; the Banach base is perfect uniform over an analytic field. General base maps give functorial maps, not a universal uncompleted tensor identity.
proofSteps: Lift rational inequalities by Teichmuller representatives.
Apply stable uniformity and the spectral-norm isometry criterion to the map from the rational localization.
The dense coefficient subring proves surjectivity and the rational base-cover assertion.
For interval covers use controlled splitting/intersections to check the gluing square, or descend the rational-cover argument after the specified perfectoid scalar extension.

nodes.statement: On M(R̃^(int,r)) the stable-presentation construction defines H(β,u), u∈[0,1], with H(β,0)=β, H(β,1)=λμ(β), μH(β,u)=μ(β), and H(H(β,u),v)=H(β,max(u,v)). It is continuous. On T_R=⋃_(0<s<r)M(R̃^[s,r]) it gives a strong deformation retract to M(R)×(0,∞). The properly discontinuous φ^d action scales the exponent by q=p^d, has compact Hausdorff quotient X_R, and descends the retraction to M(R)×(R_>0/q^Z)≃M(R)×S^1.

Check the endpoint, restriction and max-semigroup formulas.

nodes.statement: If R→S is bounded between perfect uniform Banach F_p-algebras and M(S)→M(R) is surjective, then M(R̃_S^(int,r))→M(R̃_R^(int,r)) is surjective for every r>0. No faithfully flat tensor-product hypothesis is substituted for the given spectral surjectivity.

nodes.title: Finite etale compatibility of period rings
nodes.statement: Finite etale S/R lifts to the relative Witt and extended period rings. FÉt(R̃^int)→FÉt(W(R))→FÉt(R) are tensor equivalences; at a fixed r the category is φ^−1-equivariant FÉt(R̃^(int,r)), with quasi-inverse S↦R̃_S^(int,r). The bounded and completed period-ring extensions of KL5.5.4 are finite etale and satisfy its finite-module base-change comparisons. For a normalized degree-one primitive z with z_0∈R× and z−[z_0]∈pW(R^+)×, r≥1 and intervals containing 1, the listed period-ring maps become isomorphisms modulo z^m, m>0. Consequently the lifted finite-etale correspondence agrees with the imported perfectoid tilting correspondence.
hypotheses: The fixed-radius integral category requires Frobenius descent. The primitive quotient is normalized and is taken at a window containing its radius.
Use the corrected primitive definition in KLII Appendix A: z_0 is a unit of R. This concerns the generic quotient comparison and does not remove the π=0 integral leg.

In the iterative proof of Lemma 5.5.2 initialize the residual with z_0=z, not the printed z_0=0 (source finding E11). Also use the S-period ring for the final arbitrary element in Lemma5.5.2 (E13), and read the scalar ring of Proposition5.5.3 without the printed FÉt wrapper (E14).
Use henselian lifting for the integral union and Frobenius iteration for each fixed radius.
Lift a finite-projective splitting and prove the completed tensor map is isometric.

Use the primitive relation to exchange p and [z_0] in the finite quotients; induct on m via regularity. Use the corrected x_0 coefficient and spectral coefficient norm in the final estimate of KL5.5.5 (KLII Appendix A).
Compare the finite-etale equivalence with the P3 almost-purity supplier, without rebuilding almost purity.

The relative-curve functor carries etale, finite etale and faithfully finite etale base morphisms to morphisms with the same property. The projection of underlying topological spaces upgrades to a morphism of etale topoi. This does not supply a structural adic map X_S→S.

proofSteps: Glue rational period sheaves by functoriality on overlaps.
Use the R3 etale comparison and KL8.2.21 to identify etale values.
Apply period-ring finite-etale compatibility on annuli and descend along Frobenius.
Reduce general etale morphisms to finite-etale affinoid neighborhoods and compose the induced maps of sites.
Use the corrected factorization in KL8.2.20: Z_ij→Y is finite etale and Y_ij→Z_ij is an open immersion (KLII Appendix A, p. 191).

nodes.title: Lubin–Tate diamond presentation
nodes.statement: For the perfect characteristic-p field F tilt of the Lubin–Tate tower E_LT∞, the associated classical generic period space has diamond Y_F^◇≃Spd(F)×Spd(E), equivalently the punctured perfectoid open-disc presentation of FF18 Remark3.19. The relative curve is its φ^Z quotient. The LT-tower presentation uses the O_E× action supplied by Lubin–Tate theory and local reciprocity; it is separate from the whole π/[ϖ] root extension used to prove integral chart perfectoidness.
hypotheses: This is the field-case comparison in the source. The LT torsion tower, its tilt and reciprocity are precise missing upstream inputs; no universal base or root/LT tower identification is assumed.
proofSteps: Use the formal-group torsion tower and its tilted open-disc coordinate.
Apply the reviewed diamond product description to the field pair.
Track the coefficient action and Frobenius orbit on both presentations.
Compare the resulting quotient with the RF1 curve presentation.
acceptance: Keep E_LT∞ and E_root∞ as distinct named extensions.

nodes.title: Stein exhaustion of the generic period space
nodes.statement: For affinoid perfectoid S, the generic Y_S admits a countable increasing exhaustion by compact rational annuli. Each annulus is sheafy and O-acyclic. Restriction maps on analytic functions have dense image, and the controlled annular approximations imply lim^1=0 for the countable inverse system. Hence H^i(Y_S,O)=0 for i>0 and O(Y_S) is its Frechet inverse limit. For general S this is applied on affinoid base charts, rather than asserting global acyclicity over a nonaffinoid base.
hypotheses: Affinoid base and a countable cofinal annular exhaustion. The topological inverse-limit argument uses dense restrictions and complete Banach spaces, not algebraic Mittag–Leffler surjectivity.
proofSteps: Choose cofinal intervals tending to both ends of the generic radius range.
Apply relatively perfectoid annular sheafiness and Tate acyclicity.
Approximate restrictions by the common dense bounded period subring.
Use a geometrically convergent correction sequence to kill the lim^1 obstruction, and the covering spectral sequence to conclude higher O-acyclicity.
acceptance: No unproved vanishing for an arbitrary nonaffinoid base, and no automatic surjectivity of dense restrictions.

sources.match: The source assertion concerns generic Y_S for affinoid S; the annular proof explains the scope.

nodes.title: Crystalline boundary and twist section input
nodes.statement: In FSII.2.5 put Y_[1,∞]={|[ϖ]|≤|π|≠0}, including the end [ϖ]=0,π≠0, and Y_[0,a]={|π|^a≤|[ϖ]|≠0}, retaining the end π=0. Write B_[a,b] for the rings of functions with the specified rational completion. The two-chart Cech sequences are 0→W_OE(R^+)[1/π]→B_[1,∞]⊕B_[0,q][1/π]→B_[1,q]→0 and the same sequence with q replaced by1. The coefficient ring on the left has its π-adic Tate topology, distinct from the (π,[ϖ])-adic topology of the integral period space. For n>0 the contracting Frobenius series used in FSII.2.5 give the restriction quasi-isomorphism of the two φ−π^n complexes. This provides the section input for the rank-one twists; general bundle cohomology and global generation remain at VB1/VB2.
hypotheses: Affinoid perfectoid base, actual boundary charts and their complete topologies. The notation [1,∞] does not mean a subset of generic Y. The displayed rational inequality for general a is interpreted by integer powers for rational a.
proofSteps: Apply sheafiness of the π-adic Tate ring W_OE(R^+)[1/π] to its two rational charts.
Use the exact two-chart covering sequences with q and with1.
On the integral-end term invert φ−π^n using Σ_(j≥1)π^(n(j−1))φ^(−j); on the [ϖ]-divisible crystalline-end term use −Σ_(j≥0)π^(−n(j+1))φ^j.
Check convergence in the actual interval norms and deduce the restriction quasi-isomorphism.
acceptance: This records the boundary chart calculation without importing VB2 global generation into RF3.

nodes.statement: Uniformizer and topologically nilpotent-unit choices give canonical identifications of Y_S and its sheaf; the annular coverings change by cofinal refinement with the transformed radius convention. Finite coefficient-field change is computed from the perfect unramified-base Witt tensor comparison, then rational localization, completion and integral closure of plus rings. In the specialization E=Q_p,S=Spa(F,O_F), identify each closed interval ring and plus ring with the absolute B^I,B^{I,+} of upstream AdicSpaces layer6, respecting all rational restriction maps, complete topologies and Frobenius. hypotheses: For coefficient change choose the residue embedding and corresponding q-power Frobenius. For a general completed coefficient extension use the integral coefficient-tensor interface requested from R0; no tensor product over R of nonadditive Teichmuller maps is formed.
proofSteps: Use ghost-preserving Witt uniformizer transport and the unit change in each primitive equation.
Compare the valuations defining the two annular bases and obtain cofinal rational refinements.
Carry the finite unramified-base scalar comparison through the finite completed chart operations and plus-ring integral closure.
At the fixed-field anchor match the same Witt coefficient norms and dense subrings; the completion universal property identifies the rings, not merely their Spa sets.
Check each comparison commutes with restrictions, the transported Frobenius and the F0 choice transport.

nodes.title: Local generation on period annuli
nodes.statement: Let M be finite projective over R̃^[s,r],0<s≤r. If elements e_1,…,e_n generate its base change to R̃_(H(β))^[s,r] for β∈M(R), then they generate M after a rational localization of the base (R,R^+) encircling β. This is a local neighborhood conclusion and does not assert that M is free or that the same generators work over the whole base.
hypotheses: Finite projective interval module, a finite proposed generating set and generation over the completed coefficient residue field.
proofSteps: Apply Nakayama at each point of the residue-field period annulus.
Cover that compact annulus by finitely many rational neighborhoods where the elements generate.
Spread this finite covering to a rational base neighborhood of β.
Use the residue-point detection criterion for surjectivity of finite modules to conclude generation.
acceptance: This supplies the exact PAPER-KEDLAYA-LIU-15/191 target. Global sections generating every interval are the separate VB1-owned Lemma6.1.4.

Clear source, dependency, API and Lean corrections applied in place. checked.note: FF2017 Lemma1.2.1: finite ghost polynomials on all coefficient algebras. No perfection or ghost injectivity is smuggled into the definition; polynomial naturality is routine.
FF2017 Dwork argument: cancel π recursively, with a coefficient-fixing Frobenius lift and π-regularity. No unjustified completeness hypothesis; Lean retains the two nonroutine algebraic hypotheses.

FF2017 Lemma1.2.1 constructs polynomial operations before specialization to torsion algebras. Added Witt-coordinate constructor/extensionality, coordinate-map simp and identity/composition API, with matching Lean forms.

FF2017 uniformizer comparison preserves ghosts, not coordinates. Universal torsion-free construction and natural specialization justify the cocycle; the unit factor in the V test has the correct direction.
FF2017 Lemma1.2.2: FV=π on arbitrary algebras; VF=π is restricted to residue algebras. Teichmuller multiplicativity is correctly distinguished from additivity.
FF2017 V-truncations and unique expansion: images are ideals by the projection formula. The packet explicitly distinguishes V-adic from π-adic completeness without perfection.

The all-E strict-lift prose is correct, but strictLift_equalChar uses the same ramifiedWitt carrier with no characteristic restriction. At OE=ℤ,π=q=2,A=F₂ it conflicts with ramifiedWitt_p_typical: W₂(F₂) has characteristic zero, while F₂[[T]] has characteristic two. Add an actual all-E strict-lift carrier/characteristic interface; the strict_lift_fq test also needs completeness and the specified uniformizer/residue cardinality.

FF2017/2018 Lemma1.2.3: ghost subsequence fn, uF^f=F′u and the iterate before u in the V identity. Confirmed E2 and the corrected source copy; coefficient-extension geometric context is explicitly deferred.

FF2017 diagonal is characterized by outer ghosts F^n, not a coordinate diagonal. The unramified scalar action has its stated residue-extension context; a full coefficient interface remains required as advertised.

FF2017 perfect coefficient change tensors over the maximal unramified subextension. Finite freeness controls completeness. Equal characteristic is a separate power-series argument, not arbitrary-algebra ghost theory.

FF2017 twisted ghosts require Q≡X^q modπ. Lean twistedWittEquiv and qTwistedWittFunctor omit this existing polynomial condition and claim the comparison for every Q. Add the congruence and transport it through the construction/API; the ordinary/torsion specializations alone do not enforce it.

The transported Q-Teichmuller prose matches FF2017, including nonmultiplicativity and the V expansion. Its Lean construction inherits the missing Q congruence, and qTeich_limit lacks the stated perfect-residue completion data. This is not resolved by supplying an arbitrary ambient topology.

FF2017 formal-group identities use evaluations of one specified convergent LT law. Lean ltTeich_add/scalar instead universally quantify independent lawA/lawW and scalar actions. Different constant target laws give incompatible equations. Supply the requested formal-group owner and evaluated law maps; do not add the conclusion as a hypothesis.

FF2017 weak topology is the coefficient product topology and equals the (π,[ϖ])-adic topology for a valued perfect field. The endpoint warning concerns the norm restriction, not a source theorem claiming ordinary π-adic convergence.

The chart prose correctly inverts [ϖ] and retains π=0. chart_not_witt_tate repeats a chart-unit assertion and cannot catch a definition that falsely makes the original weak Witt ring Tate. At least three discriminating tests must be represented faithfully, including the non-Tate original ring distinction.

Corrected rootChart_roots to use newly constructed rootChartRatio, and E1 fixes the whole ratio π/[ϖ]. However rootChart_tiltCoordinate still quantifies unrelated pm,vm,sm; rootChart_reduce has unrelated quotient/model arguments. root_reciprocal only says zero is not a unit. Link the actual coefficient roots and tilt presentation; source E1 must remain reflected in a discriminating chart test.

FSII.1.1: nonvanishing of [ϖ], gluing of rational charts, choice independence and q-Frobenius give the integral domain. Pinned spa is used only as the valuation subset, not as an already constructed adic space.

FSII.1.2 functor-of-points identifies the marked untilt coefficient map. Made D6 request explicitly an extension by SW pre-adic §§18.1–18.2, rather than claiming existing D6 supplies Spd(OE); RT-padic-1/3 remains honestly unresolved at its owner.

FSII.1.3 glues the affinoid construction over perfectoid base opens, with restriction compatibility. The displayed Lean open-preimage fragment is legitimate under §13 but is not a claim that gluing is implemented.

Ked-Ainf Hyp3.4/Def3.5: remove simultaneous vanishing, keeping both analytic ends and their different Tate completions. Tests distinguish this locus from the generic intersection; the scope is explicitly p-typical.
Ked-Ainf3.6 and SW13.1.1–3: exact stably-uniform chart list, no stronger claim about A2 and no relative strong-noetherian assertion. Continuous split perfectoid extensions feed the stated R5 owner.

Ked-Ainf3.8 and GR4.15: finite locally free pullback equivalence on punctured algebraic/analytic loci. The field-only extension/freeness theorem3.9 is separated, with Example3.14 guarding general bases.

FSII.1.8 root extension and tilt yield a continuous topological map, without an additive ring embedding. Classical equation π−[a] and marking recovery agree with source; future geometric locus parameters are explicitly identified.

FSII.1.10 requires a convergent nonzero power series and its Gauss norm. Lean gaussDiscFibre quantifies any function f and any bound, including bound=0, and would conclude a nonnegative valuation is <0. FSII.1.9 concerns the entire fibre being one classical point. Corrected Lean from uniqueness among classical lifts to a classical y with the whole fibre equal to {y}; retained the nonclassical assertion only for rank-one points.

FSII.1.15 generic domain removes π=0 from the integral domain, equivalently both factors are nonzero. The packet keeps it distinct from the whole analytic locus and uses coefficient functoriality.

FSII.1.16 uses the rank-one generalization for the real logarithmic radius and rational power inequalities for higher rank. Equal endpoints and changed pseudouniformizer scaling are retained; the arbitrary Frobenius stand-in requires the stated q-Frobenius context.

FSII.1.15–16: radius scaling proves free totally discontinuous action; analytic quotient glues wandering charts. qcqs is restricted to affinoid S in the packet. The prototype’s compactness fragment does not prove quasi-separatedness; its omitted geometry is explicit.

FSII.1.17: product and equivariant quotient formulas preserve the coefficient/base action. Only a qcqs continuous topological projection is claimed; no adic structural morphism X→S is introduced. Fixed-Qp F1/F2 are compatibility imports only.

FSII.1.3/II.1.16: functorial coefficient maps descend equivariantly. Ordinary cartesian adic squares over S are explicitly excluded; the product statement is on diamonds. No tensor over a nonadditive Teichmuller map is used.

FSII.1.4 primitive theta kernel is an all-E extension, with P1 p-typical correspondence imported directly. It includes ξ=π on a characteristic-p integral leg and uses multiplicative Teichmuller, not Q/LT lifts.

FSII.1.4–5 lower bound gives regularity and closed complete quotient. Corrected the maximum-modulus proof to finite-type ordinary disc approximations and boundary suprema, then limits; the R0 theorem is not applied wholesale to a perfected/non-noetherian chart.

It does not discriminate the forbidden definition. Test quotient/sheafification and stabilizer information at a repeated leg.

Sch13Lemma6.3 and the Cartier construction: I^n/I^(n+1) is a line and tensor powers of I/I². The suggested module quotient is correctly formed through Submodule.comap, rather than a ring quotient of a nonunital ideal.
